mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when FEDFUNDS declines, with statistical significance (p<0.05) over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when UNRATE increases by >0.3pp, with p>0.05 in t-tests.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicate demand contraction amid inflation, triggering equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST decline + CPI rise) fails to predict negative returns in >40% of cases over 3-year rolling windows (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%), rising interest rates compress equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0%, with p>0.05 in regime-specific t-tests.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 signals strong labor market growth that boosts consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in >60% of months with PAYEMS growth >100k, with p>0.05 in rolling window analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production (INDPRO) decline below 105.0 signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >60% of months when INDPRO falls below 105.0, with p>0.05 in regime-specific tests.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent quarterly GDP (GDPC1) decline and monthly housing starts (HOUST) drop signal broad economic weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (GDPC1 decline + HOUST drop) fails to predict negative returns in >40% of 60-day windows over 3-year rolling periods.

mechanism_narrative: High-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY) pressure central banks to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >60% of months when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, with p>0.05 in regime-specific analysis.
